claims.text: Local server. Because nothing leaves the machine, Ollama is trusted with IP, is AGENTIC (drives its own file reads), and MAY WRITE -- but with reduced rights vs Claude: the write-guard blocks device/vendor/secret/high-risk paths, it only writes when the router grants write mode, and it is confined to repo_root.
claims.why: The claim about trust, write-guard behavior, router, and repo_root confinement refers to code outside this chunk (e.g., write-guard, router). Cannot verify here.

claims.text: DEFAULT_HOST = "http://127.0.0.1:11434"  # not "localhost" -- avoids IPv6 (::1) miss on Windows
claims.why: The constant DEFAULT_HOST is exactly that string. The comment explains the choice; no contradiction in this chunk.
The claim that this model is the default per docs/PROVIDERS_RESEARCH.md cannot be checked because that file is not in this chunk.

claims.text: BEFORE CHANGING THIS, KNOW WHAT THE AXIS ACTUALLY IS. Measured 2026-07-29 on an RTX 5080, 3 trials x 2 agent-shaped tasks per model, native `tools` array: ...
claims.why: The claim about empirical measurements, model performance, and _schema_rescue refers to data and code outside this chunk. Cannot verify.

claims.text: How long Ollama keeps the model resident in VRAM after a request. Ollama's default is 5 minutes; past that the next chat turn pays a full reload (measured ~44s cold vs ~1.4s warm first token for qwen2.5-coder:7b on this box). Override with OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE (any Ollama duration string, e.g. "10m", "2h", "-1" for forever, "0" to disable pinning).
claims.why: The claim about Ollama's default keep-alive, measured reload times, and env var override refers to external behavior and possibly other code; not verifiable in this chunk.

claims.text: MAX_REWRITE_FILES = 3       # scoped writes only; bigger fan-outs go through Ikarus
claims.why: The comment mentions Ikarus, which is not in this chunk. The constant value is kept.

claims.text: MAX_REWRITE_CHARS = 24_000  # full-file rewrite above this risks truncation
claims.why: Constant defined as 24_000. The comment about truncation risk is a claim about behavior not verifiable here.

claims.text: MEASURED 2026-07-29, the first live self-improvement runs: three docref attempts against docs/HANDOFF.md (2496 lines / 148_291 bytes) all ended no_change/write_gate_failed. The file never reached the model -- 148 KB is 6x MAX_REWRITE_CHARS, so _run_rewrite skipped it "too large for full rewrite" and the write gate correctly saw no diff. Raising the cap does not fix it: the rewrite-only reliability finding was measured on SMALL files, and a 7B model asked to reprint 2500 lines echoes or truncates.
claims.why: Claims about specific runs, file size, and _run_rewrite behavior refer to code and data outside this chunk. Cannot verify.

claims.text: MAX_WINDOW_LINES = 400      # past this it is a full rewrite wearing a window's name
Marker appended when a tool result is head-truncated to make the forced final report call fit the local context window (visible so the model knows it lost tail).
claims.why: The claim about when and how _TOOL_TRUNC_MARKER is used refers to code outside this chunk. The constant is defined.
The namedtuple is defined with those fields.

Several constants (MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS, etc.) are imported from other modules but not defined in this chunk; they are used in comments but not in code here.
